enonce_intro_markdown: Given the sets $Q=\{x;\ x \text{ is a factor of } 18\}$ and $R=\{x:\ x \text{ is a multiple of } 3 \text{ less than } 18\}$.
incertitudes: Q4 : R est lu comme l'ensemble des multiples POSITIFS de 3 inférieurs à 18 (0 exclu), soit {3, 6, 9, 12, 15}. Le sujet ne le précise pas. Le diagramme de Venn est à tracer par l'élève : le corrigé le décrit (éléments de chaque zone).

questions.corrige_markdown:
The factors of $18$ are the whole numbers that divide $18$ exactly: $18=1\times18=2\times9=3\times6$.

**$Q=\{1,2,3,6,9,18\}$.**

The multiples of $3$ less than $18$ are $3\times1,3\times2,\dots$ up to $3\times5=15$ (since $3\times6=18$ is not less than $18$).

**$R=\{3,6,9,12,15\}$.**

$Q\cap R$ is the set of elements that belong to both $Q$ and $R$.

Common elements of $\{1,2,3,6,9,18\}$ and $\{3,6,9,12,15\}$: $3$, $6$ and $9$.

**$Q\cap R=\{3,6,9\}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Draw a Venn diagram to represent the two sets. *[7 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Draw a rectangle for the universal set, and inside it two overlapping circles, one labelled $Q$ and one labelled $R$.

Place the elements in the three regions:

| Region | Elements |
|---|---|
| In $Q$ only (left part of circle $Q$) | $1,\ 2,\ 18$ |
| In both $Q$ and $R$ (overlap) | $3,\ 6,\ 9$ |
| In $R$ only (right part of circle $R$) | $12,\ 15$ |

Check: $n(Q)=3+3=6$ elements in $Q$ and $n(R)=3+2=5$ elements in $R$, which agrees with parts (a) and (b).
